newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco Chile decision due mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco Chile decision due mid-1997.

text.p: Australian aluminium producer Comalco Ltd said on Wednesday that a decision on whether to go ahead with a joint venture hydro-powered aluminium smelter in southern Chile would be made around the middle of 1997.
"A decision whether or not to proceed with the project could be made around the middle of 1997," Comalco spokesman Ian Head said in a statement.
Comalco earlier on Wednesday said it planned to take a 50 percent share of Noranda Inc's hydro-powered Alumysa smelter project in southern Chile.
It said a planned expansion of the project could involve US$2.5 billion in new investment.

Comalco said Noranda had bought water rights sufficient to supply a 270,000 tonne reduction plant, but since then there had been over-capacity in the aluminium industry due primarily to sharply reduced internal demand in the former Soviet Union.

Now that aluminium demand had continued to grow in the rest of the world, particularly in transportation and packaging applications, Noranda and Comalco believed that additional capacity would be needed in the next few years.
It said the companies were evaluating the possibility of expanding Alumysa's potential capacity to 420,000 tonnes a year by acquiring more water rights.
"Pending successful feasiblity studies an expanded project would amount to a total capital investment approaching US$2.5 billion," Comalco said.
A Chilean power company may participate in the ownership and operationof the hydro-electric facilities.
Preliminary studies for the expanded project and discussions with the Chilean government related to the additional water rights were underway, Comalco said.
Comalco shares were 15 cents higher at A$7.05 at 1.10 pm (0310 GMT).
